prompt: A colleague wrote this in two steps with a subquery in FROM: step 1 counts the orders of each store, and step 2 averages those counts for each store type. Only stores with at least one order count. Which query writes the same two steps with a CTE (WITH) and returns the right answer, with the columns store_type and avg_orders?

options.text:
WITH store_orders AS (
  -- one row per store type
  SELECT s.store_type, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders o
  JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
  GROUP BY s.store_type
)
SELECT store_type, AVG(n_orders) AS avg_orders
FROM store_orders
GROUP BY store_type

WITH store_orders AS (
  -- one row per store
  SELECT o.store_id, s.store_type, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders o
  JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
  GROUP BY o.store_id, s.store_type
)
SELECT store_type, AVG(n_orders) AS avg_orders
FROM store_orders
GROUP BY store_type

WITH store_orders AS (
  -- one row per store
  SELECT o.store_id, s.store_type, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
  GROUP BY o.store_id, s.store_type
)
SELECT store_type, AVG(n_orders) AS avg_orders
FROM store_orders
GROUP BY store_type

WITH store_orders AS (
  -- one row per store
  SELECT s.store_id, s.store_type, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM stores s
  LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.store_id
  GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_type
)
SELECT store_type, AVG(n_orders) AS avg_orders
FROM store_orders
GROUP BY store_type
